hints: Notice the flow rate is $90 \text{ kg per minute}$ but the water speed $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ is per second, so the time units must match.
Connect the holding force to the rate of gain of forward momentum by the water, $F = \text{(mass per second)} \times \text{change in velocity}$.
First divide $90 \text{ kg}$ by $60 \text{ s}$ to get $\text{kg s}^{-1}$, then multiply that mass rate by $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to get force in newtons.
walkthrough: Identify the physics: water initially in the pipe gains horizontal momentum as it is ejected at $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the pipe feels an equal backward rate of momentum change.
Convert the mass flow rate to SI units: $\frac{\Delta m}{\Delta t} = \frac{90 \text{ kg}}{60 \text{ s}} = 1.5 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$.
State the governing rule: force equals rate of change of momentum, $F = \frac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \frac{\Delta m}{\Delta t} \times v$.
Substitute values with units: $F = 1.5 \text{ kg s}^{-1} \times 20 \text{ m s}^{-1} = 30 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$.
Check units: $1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2} = 1 \text{ N}$, so $F = 30 \text{ N}$ forward momentum per second, requiring $30 \text{ N}$ backward hold. This is option A.
